case_title: Amrutlal Liladharbhai Kotak v. State of Gujarat
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (husband) and in-laws (Relative: husband's family, including parents-in-law)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.498-A, s.304-B, s.306 read with s.114; Evidence Act s.113-A and s.113-B referred to
evidence_type: Testimonial (complainant, elder sister, grandfather, friend of deceased); documentary (photographs of body, inquest panchnama); post-mortem examination
aggravating_circumstances: Repeated dowry demands from date of marriage; mental torture and harassment for insufficient dowry; death by suicide within seven years of marriage
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.498-A, 304-B and 306 read with s.114; sentence not stated in the judgment
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; trial court conviction and sentence upheld
offence_finally_established: IPC s.498-A, s.304-B and s.306 read with s.114 (dowry death, cruelty and abetment of suicide), as upheld
neutral_facts: The victim, a married woman living in a joint household with her husband and his parents and relatives at Morbi, was found hanging from a ceiling fan at the marital home on 23 March 2000. A family member of the accused telephoned the victim's father, who worked at a bank in Rajkot, to come to the house. The police were informed, and an assistant sub-inspector visited the scene, recorded a statement from the accused's family member, and initially registered the death as accidental. The investigation was then taken over by an inspector. The victim's father arrived later that day and suspected foul play, noting that the accused had repeatedly demanded dowry and that none of them were present at the house when the death occurred. A complaint was lodged and an FIR registered for offences relating to cruelty, dowry death and abetment of suicide. The body was cut down and sent for post-mortem examination. Several witnesses were examined. The victim's father, elder sister and grandfather testified that the victim frequently complained of mental torture and harassment by the accused for bringing insufficient dowry. A close friend of the victim testified that the victim had told her of such harassment. Photographs of the body and the inquest panchnama were placed on record. The accused had absconded for some weeks before surrendering at the police station.
physical_harm: Death of the victim by hanging (suicide)
motive: Demand for dowry and mental harassment of the deceased for insufficient dowry
key_evidence_accepted: Testimony of PW-1 (complainant), PW-7 (friend of deceased), PW-8 (elder sister) and PW-9 (grandfather); documentary evidence including photographs and inquest panchnama
witness_credibility: Court accepted the version of PW-1, PW-7, PW-8 and PW-9 as establishing a reasonable apprehension of crime; the defence argument that relatives are interested witnesses was not accepted
post_offence_conduct: Absconded for 36 days; surrendered at Morbi City Police Station on 29.04.2000
trial_duration: offence: 23.03.2000; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 17.06.2009; Supreme Court: 26.02.2015
legal_representation: Accused: K. T. S. Tulsi, Huzefa Ahmadi and others. State of Gujarat: Nitin Sangra, Hemantika Wahi and others
investigation_status: Initially registered as accidental death (A.O. No.16/2000); FIR/CR No.92/2000 registered for ss.498-A, 304-B, 306 r/w 114 IPC; investigation completed; trial held
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.498-A, 304-B, 306 r/w 114 IPC. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction upheld (17.06.2009). Supreme Court: appeal dismissed (26.02.2015)
defence_argument: Prosecution failed to prove abetment or incitement to suicide (Kishori Lal); mere cruelty is insufficient; witnesses were interested; cruelty immediately before death not established; absconding alone cannot prove guilt (Matru)
legal_principle_applied: ss.304-B and 498-A are not mutually inclusive; presumption under s.113-B Evidence Act where suicide occurs within seven years of marriage; presumption under s.113-A of abetment where cruelty by husband or relatives immediately preceded suicide
precedent_relied_upon: Balwant Singh v. State of Himachal Pradesh (2008) 15 SCC 497; State of Punjab v. Iqbal Singh (1991) 3 SCC 1; Dinesh v. State of Haryana (2014) 5 SCALE 641; Thanu Ram v. State of M.P. (2010) 10 SCC 353
judicial_aggravating_factors: Suicide within seven years of marriage; cruelty and dowry-related harassment immediately before death
